question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated control over the Chinese Communist Party, military, and state institutions underpins the 95.7% trader consensus that he will remain in power through 2026. Since abolishing presidential term limits in 2018, he has maintained authority through repeated anti-corruption purges that have removed senior Politburo and military figures, ensuring loyalty among remaining elites. No designated successor has emerged, and official signals point to his continued leadership at the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027. Ongoing cadre reshuffles and the absence of visible factional challenges reinforce this positioning ahead of the next leadership transition cycle. Health developments, an unforeseen elite revolt, or a major external crisis could still alter the timeline, though none appear imminent based on current reporting.
